topic: Specialized Structures of Terrestrial and Aquatic Plants
key_concepts: Terrestrial plants grow on land and get nutrients from air and soil
Aquatic plants live in water and may be submersed or emersed
Waxy leaves protect plants from dehydration
Cactus has fleshy and thorny stems to store water
Thorns and hairs are protective structures
Some fruits and flowers use strong odors to attract pollinators
Thick cuticle filters strong light and reduces water loss
Sharp leaves and spines protect plants from harm
Aquatic plants have flat buoyant leaves and air sacs for flotation
Long or feathery roots help aquatic plants reach soil or take in oxygen
Specialized structures help plants adapt to particular habitats
